abstract: Reza Alavi MBCS, Chair of BCS IRMA (Information Risk Management and Assurance Group) and Cyber Security & Risk Consultant at Wipro-Cloud looks at getting the cyber basics right when working from home.

articleTitle: Getting Bitten by the Love Bug
abstract: Twenty years ago, millions of people fell victim to the Love Bug worm. Prof Steven Furnell FBCS looks back at the incident and considers how things have changed since.

The paper ‘Will I Regret This Tweet? — Twitter User's Behaviour Analysis System for Private Data Disclosure’, by R Geetha, S Karthika and Ponnurangam Kumaraguru published online in The Computer Journal, May 2020, explores how private tweets could be searchable in a variety of defined domains.

articleTitle: The Unresolved Challenge of Computers and the Older Generation

abstract: Rachel Steenson FBCS explores how innovative cartographic visualisation technologies are helping countries, governments and NGOs combat coronavirus.
As technology gains pace, the mix of capital and labour is transforming the way industrial economies are structured and managed, writes Dr John McManus MBCS.

articleTitle: Accelerating Change How Covid-19 Changed the Industry
abstract: Covid-19 continues to be a true and growing global crisis. The BCS Content Team explores how the virus has placed huge pressures on IT teams, forced leadership to adapt and driven transformation forward in ways we couldn’t previously have imagined.

articleTitle: Most Influential Women in UK Tech
abstract: BCSWomen feature in Computer Weekly's Most Influential Women in UK Tech 2020 longlist. BCS President Rebecca George OBE reacts.

The theme for the autumn issue of ITNOW is, unsurprisingly, based around the rapid change of pace faced by all in the IT profession as a result of the Covid-19 pandemic, writes Ian Fish, Chair of the Information Security Specialist Group (ISSP).
Darren Watkins, Managing Director for VIRTUS Data Centres offers his advice for working remotely and maintaining business continuity as the UK goes into lockdown.
Going through this experience of Covid-19 as a society has changed us all forever, writes Giacomo Mosca FBCS, a global leader in management consultancy. But what have we learned?
BCS’ strategy of making relevant public interventions based on data and insight is beginning to make an impact, thanks to strong membership support, writes James Woodward, Head of Policy and PR.

The image of the computer science teacher as the ‘solitary geek’ in the staffroom is undergoing a dramatic change as they become the go-to person as schools figure out how to deliver lessons online. Computing teachers have been helping colleagues across the curriculum take the practical steps needed to set up remote learning. BCS Senior Press Officer Claire Penketh reports.

Visualisation is an incredibly powerful tool for communicating business change. Our perception of the world is overwhelmingly visual, with 50% of our mental energy typically spent on processing this information, writes Jonathan Whelan FBCS.

Take time to understand how the human brain works — writes Carole Osterweil, Project Troubleshooter and Author of Project Delivery, Uncertainty and Neuroscience — A Leader's Guide to Walking in Fog — and you can enjoy higher productivity and better project outcomes with less complexity and less stress.
When Rob Greig FBCS joined Arup as CIO, he was told that a transformation of the IT team had been tried before and would never succeed. Rob tells Johanna Hamilton AMBCS why he begged to differ.

On 23 March 2020, Boris Johnson announced that to tackle Covid-19 and protect the NHS, a UK lockdown would begin with immediate effect. IT workers all over the country sprang into action to keep the country running; BCS wanted to ensure their actions were recognised, writes Johanna Hamilton AMBCS.

In February 2001, at a mountain lodge in Utah, seventeen people met to eat, drink, ski and talk about their work. Over the course of three days, they found common ground in their different approaches and wrote down 68 words to describe them. Those 68 words form The Agile Manifesto, writes Simon Girvan.

articleTitle: Once Upon a Time… Storytelling For Cybersecurity
abstract: After the ubiquity of internet access for children of all ages during the Covid-19 lockdown, BCS Author Wendy Goucher harnesses the power of stories to open a conversation about cyber security.

A global pandemic is a traumatic place to be. Among many other things, the fact that the university is physically closed may promote worries about the progress of your degree, writes Blay Whitby MBCS, Lecturer in Cognitive Science for the University of Sussex.

Our international hubs are located across Europe, North America, Asia and Africa, supporting our member communities in these areas with a platform for networking, professional development and debate. Guy Sergio Arlapen FBCS CITP, Chair of the Mauritius International Section, completes the ITNOW Q&A about the group.

Earlier this year, the 13th BCSWomen Lovelace Colloquium for undergraduate and MSc women in computing was held. Hosted by the University of Stirling with support from the University of Glasgow, Dr Hannah Dee, Senior Lecturer in Computer Science at Aberystwyth University, tells ITNOW about the event.

articleTitle: The Gem of All Mechanisms: Computing in Society
abstract: The Gem of all Mechanisms: Computing in society is an interview series, where we talk to people in the know about the complexities of 21st century tech and how it affects us all. Martin Cooper MBCS discusses the podcast series’ recent successes.

articleTitle: EU Project to Quantum Make Mainstream
abstract: Hannes Huebel, Senior Scientist in the Security & Communications Technologies unit at the Austrian Institute of Technology, talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about the need to bring three decades of quantum research out of the lab and into the mainstream.

In March this year, it became clear that BCS insights 2020 wouldn’t be able to take place at The Crystal in London as planned. in fact, not much of 2020 would be happening as planned! And so a new plan was made: with a team of dedicated professionals taking care of the logistics and a panel of speakers who showed great humility and flexibility, we went virtual.

Big data is one of the newer threads within the technology industry, writes Paul Taylor MBCS, author and IT consultant. However, like most things, big data is a not a silver bullet; it has a number of challenges that people need to be aware of.

Sir Desmond Pitcher FBCS has worked on both sides of the Atlantic and all sides of the IT industry. In this interview with The Archives of IT, he talks about growing up in war torn Liverpool, his education and a long and varied career, culminating in a knighthood for his services to the people of Liverpool.

articleTitle: Building a Secure Messaging App For The NHS
abstract: Through careful adherence to GDPR and a dogged focus on providing just what doctors and nurses need — and no more — start-up company Hospify believes its app can help clinicians communicate smartly and securely. Martin Cooper MBCS reports.

‘MSN fires its human editors.’ This was another ‘AI will take your job’ scare story. And, as night follows day, the AI made a high-profile error hours later, confusing mixed-race singers from a popular band. Brian Runciman MBCS reports on BCS’ latest AI research.

Kay Hardy, Senior Software Consultant at Capita Software and Deborah Garfen, Digital Product Designer at the British Heart Foundation, share their experience of working collaboratively with a variety of tools from Miro to Microsoft.

Professional body accreditation must better communicate its value to higher education institutions, industry and society as a whole. Tom Crick, James H. Davenport, Paul Hanna, Alastair Irons, Sally Pearce and Tom Prickett explore the value of - and future enhancements to - BCS accreditation.

articleTitle: Passwords a Lesson in Cyber Security Failure?
abstract: Passwords are dead, writes Steven Furnell FBCS of the Centre for Security, Communications and Network Research at the University of Plymouth. Numerous people have said so (just search for the phrase to see for yourself).

articleTitle: The SOC is Dead, Long Live the SOC!
abstract: The traditional tiered security operation centre approach is flawed, writes Matthew Smith, Global Head of Cyber Security, St. James's Palace ‐ simply because we are human. We must leverage the benefits of machine learning, user behaviour analytics and security automation to deliver effective detection and response in 2020 and beyond.

articleTitle: Cyber Security: Advice from the Front Line
abstract: Joseph Rose is a Senior Security Architect for a large financial institution. Johanna Hamilton AMBCS asks him about the challenges of cyber security for the decade and why humans pose more problems than quantum.

Is everyone talking ethics in IT right now? Combinations of anger, worry and helplessness are surely not the feelings computing wants to generate. But in 2020, there are justifiable fears about technology and plenty of misunderstanding about what it can and can't do. This year, BCS is focusing its research and main conference on what personal responsibility means in IT. Brian Runciman MBCS writes.

articleTitle: BCS Report it Leaders 2020: Change Transformation Resources
abstract: This year's IT Leaders Report lifts the lid on the pressures, decisions and future possibilities that are occupying technology leaders' minds. Martin Cooper MBCS RIT Tech looks at some of the report's defining stories.

As is the case each quarter, the ITNOW commissioning editor informed me of the genera theme of the issue ‐ for Spring 2020, it was staying well ‐ specifically promoting better mental health in the workplace, writes Ian Fish, Chair of the Information Security Specialist Group.

Under the patronage of HE Shaikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance, the BCS ICT Conference 2019 was launched, at the Anantara Eastern Mangroves Hotel, Abu Dhabi on 27th Oct under the theme: ‘Tolerance, Sustainability & Women's Empowerment’.

Wayne Smith CITP FBCS MSc, IT and Information Security Director at Birmingham Airport, talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about the benefits of taking more tech in-house, and why it's a good idea if everything isn't connected.

articleTitle: Cyber Mission Assurance for Cyber Security
abstract: Matthew Mackay, Cyber Risk Analyst at Whiteflare Consulting, explains why organisations should follow a cyber mission assurance approach (CMA) for cyber security.

Sean O'Neil from Bedfordshire Police investigates fraud and helps people and organisations avoid falling victim. He shows Martin Cooper MBCS behind the statistics as he explores the true human cost of online crime.

Pip Green, Head of Corporate Responsibility at CGI UK, explains their ‘bring your daughter to work’ initiative to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS and why it's so important to get girls into STEM subjects from an early age.

articleTitle: Surveillance and Physical Security in the Cloud
abstract: Steven Kenny, Industry Liaison Architecture and Engineering at Axis Communications and Rodrigue Zbinden, CEO at Morphean, discuss the future of connected cloud‐enabled physical security systems, the business intelligence that can be drawn from them and the obligation to meet the privacy needs of the general public.

articleTitle: Digital Badging and the Need for Assessment Framework
abstract: When it comes to evidencing skills, knowledge and experience, digital badges have indelible advantages. But, as Paul Jagger FBCS explains, there is room for improvement.

articleTitle: Coronavirus What History Can Tell us About Tomorrow
abstract: As the Covid‐19 situation evolves, Robert A. Clark FBCS looks at past pandemics and asks if there are lessons we can learn from history that will help us prepare our business and people.

articleTitle: How to Plan and Implement Change
abstract: Paul Taylor MBCS, speaker, author and mentor, discusses the essential elements needed for successful business transformation - and how sometimes it's simply the ability to deal with uncertainty that could spell the difference between success and failure.

Nancy Doyle PhD has been working with social exclusion and disabilities since she was 18 years old. She discusses why neurodiversity is a boon in the workplace and why mental health isn't necessarily a work-issue, with Johanna Hamilton AMBCS.

Peter Cox, CEO and Founder of UM Labs, explores VoIP and messaging systems and explains why organisations need to ensure high levels of security around data-in-transit, warning that failure to do so may lead to GDPR compliance issues.

The paper ‘Sound Stories: A Context-Based Study of Everyday Listening to Augmented Soundscapes' by Milena Droumeva and Iain McGregor published in Interacting with Computers, Volume 31, Issue 3, May 2019, explores how soundscapes are transforming to accommodate additional sonic feedback.

In June 2019, BCS ran an event at the Crystal in London that brought together diversity campaigners, AI experts, policymakers, ethicists and more to debate the pressing issues of IT and computing. In this most exciting of spaces, as an organisation with over 60 years' experience and a remit to make IT good for society, BCS is well placed to be a convener of views.

articleTitle: It's Easier to Talk About Diarrhoea Than Depression
abstract: People are much more comfortable talking about physical ailments than mental ones. The title of this piece comes from a blog post by the Chief Executive of Mental Health First Aid England and demonstrates well why mental health is an ongoing conversation. BCS undertook research at the end of 2019, alongside an analysis of ONS data, to see the effects in IT. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

Richard Mort is a Director at Edge Testing Solutions and an ex-contractor. He explores the issues of IR35 for contractors and discusses the pros and cons of leaving contracting behind for a permanent role.

articleTitle: BCS Director Recognised in New Year's Honours
abstract: Director of Policy at BCS, Dr Bill Mitchell, has been awarded an OBE in the New Year's Honours for services to computing and artificial intelligence education.

The eighth annual Lumen Prize, celebrating the very best in international digital art, took place at the Barbican Centre for Performing Arts in London on 24 October. Presenting the BCS AI Award to winners, Dave Murray-Rust and Rocio von Jungenfeld — for Lichtsuchende — was Computer Arts Society Chair, Dr Nick Lambert.

Craig Barber MBCS M.Inst.ISP CISSP tells ITNOW why strategic planning in cyber security is a little more challenging than you’d first think. But, get it right and you'll stand a better chance of surviving an attack.

So… that software you are currently using: what do you know about it? Writes Brian Gooch, an Independent Database Engineer, specialising in designing and creating structured computer software systems.

What do the Welsh and process improvement have in common? Gareth Baxendale FBCS CITP FEDIPLeadPract, Head of Technology at the National Institute for Health Research, explains the surprising connection.

articleTitle: What's Really Happening in Data Protection?
abstract: Jeremy Holt is the senior partner of Clark Holt Commercial Solicitors, specialising in IT law. He talks to Blair Melsom AMBCS about data breaches, Brexit and nurturing the next generation of talent.

articleTitle: 5 Steps to a Better Tech Fit in Mergers & Acquisitions
abstract: Mergers and acquisitions (M&As) are expensive activities. They are arguably the largest undertaking a business can make - and, writes Renat Zubairov CEO of elastic.io - unsuccessful attempts can be enormously costly in time, money and reputation.

When it comes to ethics and providing an essential service to do good for society, the Royal College of Nursing and BCS have much in common. Johanna Hamilton AMBCS investigates the benefits of corporate membership and how this symbiotic relationship is paying dividends.
A well-run workshop is a great way to engage a wide variety of stakeholders and can be an excellent platform for exploring ideas, engaging others and eliciting requirements, writes Rachel Drinkwater.
